images.caption: Figure 1:Supervision for data agents: exploration-based synthesis (top) versus Data World (bottom). Exploring existing files may leave valid findings without matching criteria; Data World specifies mechanisms first, aligning files and rubrics with analytical targets.

Figure 2:Data World synthesis and evaluation pipeline. A dependency DAG and world contract guide layer-wise canonical-state generation; observation projection produces analyst-visible files. An independent auditor checks relationships, invariants, and target recoverability. The generative record grounds tasks and rubrics; the data agent solves tasks from observed files, and a separate evaluator grades its report.
Figure 3:Taxonomy shares (%) of the DataWorld-Bench test tasks and Data World RL training tasks.

Table 1:DataWorld-Bench results (normalized rubric scores×100\times 100, with SD in parentheses). Avg pools all rubric items and need not equal the mean of the two section columns. Best/second-best means arebold/underlined. Rounds count model calls; tokens are prompt plus output of the final call (total) or outputs over the run (response).

Table 2:Distribution of triggered negative rubric items across trajectories.
